description: We are a team of three students interested in science, technology, physics, and engineering. We enjoy solving problems, exploring new ideas, and understanding how things work. We value logical thinking, creativity, and teamwork. We want to apply our knowledge in practice, develop new skills, and create an innovative project during the hackathon.
summary: Lunar Landing Navigator is an interactive 3D application developed to make lunar surface exploration easier and more accessible. It allows users to explore a realistic digital Moon, rotate and zoom the globe, inspect specific locations, and visualize surface imagery, elevation, illumination and shadows. Using NASA lunar datasets, including LRO WAC imagery, the application combines scientific information in one intuitive interface. Users can also adjust map layers, coordinate grids and date and time settings to investigate changing sunlight conditions across the lunar surface. The project addresses the challenge by transforming complex lunar data into an accessible visual tool for understanding potential landing environments. It is important because accurate knowledge of lunar terrain and illumination can support future exploration planning, scientific research and education about the Moon.
details: Lunar Landing Navigator is an interactive application designed to explore the Moon and investigate potential lunar landing locations. It features a realistic 3D lunar globe with NASA LRO WAC imagery, elevation data, illumination and shadow visualization. Users can rotate and zoom the Moon, select specific locations, inspect geographic coordinates and explore how sunlight changes over time. Interactive coordinate grids, adjustable map layers and date controls make lunar exploration easier and more accessible. Developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js and NASA Moon Trek services, the project aims to support space education, scientific exploration and future lunar mission planning.
